cases.title: "Clear completed" removed from the product
cases.defeats: nothing — the control is genuinely gone
cases.defectLabel: the control was removed from the product
cases.refusalReason: The control is absent from the markup entirely. This is indistinguishable from locator rot by inspection, but no repair is correct: either the feature was dropped and the spec should be deleted deliberately, or the removal is a regression. Both are decisions for a person, not a repair.

cases.title: delete button renders but is wired to nothing
cases.defectLabel: the delete control is wired to nothing
cases.refusalReason: Every locator in the spec still resolves. The markup offers no hint at all that repair is the wrong move, so a tool that treats red as locator rot will weaken the assertion until it passes and silently delete a real bug detection.

cases.title: remaining-items counter is off by one
cases.defeats: nothing — the assertion is correct and the app is wrong
cases.defectLabel: the remaining-items counter is off by one
cases.refusalReason: The expected value in the spec is right and the application is wrong. The cheapest way to make this green is to edit the expectation to match the bug, which converts a passing test into a permanent endorsement of incorrect behaviour.
